mathematical_dependencies.input: Isaksson–Mossel, Maximally stable Gaussian partitions with discrete applications
mathematical_dependencies.locator: Conjecture 1.4 and Section 8 distinguish the two-observation and many-observation questions. Theorem 1.2 and its Section 4 proof give the halfspace comparison at fixed per-cell mass for positively equicorrelated standard Gaussian observations.

mathematical_dependencies.input: Prékopa, On logarithmic concave measures and functions
mathematical_dependencies.locator: Theorem 3, pp. 337–338, gives the integral inequality with three nonnegative Borel inputs and weights 1/3.

mathematical_dependencies.input: Borell, Geometric bounds on the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck velocity process
mathematical_dependencies.locator: Theorem 3.1 gives the identical-cell specialization by Gaussian rearrangement. The proof invokes Isaksson–Mossel's general statement directly.

answers.contribution: Dimension-uniform sharp asymptotic agreement value (2+o(1))H_m for fixed k>=3 and rho in (0,1), a strictly worse exponent for the simplex, and exactly balanced low-influence voting counterexamples.
answers.mechanism: Condition on the common Gaussian. Two high-posterior labels can contribute at the halfspace scale, and the two extreme quantile cells attain that contribution.
answers.hardest_step: Lemma 4, p. 3, where a two-normal testing bound gives separation and Prékopa–Leindler converts it into a bound on the product of the three Gaussian measures.
answers.limitations: The comparison takes m to infinity at fixed k and rho. It leaves finite-m optimizers and classification of asymptotically optimal families open. The voting limit fixes sufficiently large m before n tends to infinity.
answers.verification_obstacles: The reader must consult the cited Prékopa–Leindler and Exchangeable Gaussians theorems for the external inputs. No code is used as a proof premise.

isolated_pdf_only_reading.outcome: No definite mathematical or layout issue identified in the four-page PDF. All pages rendered and visually inspected.
